cells.tense: You are here with your hand on the pen, and what you are ending is ending on purpose.
cells.act: charge forward on the decision you made
cells.ask: Take the ending you already decided on one step further — say the sentence to whoever it concerns, or carry the object that marks it out of the room.
cells.core:
You keep asking questions about what's here, turning it over, wanting to see it from every side — and the questions are landing somewhere real. In this clearing they have a floor under them. You're not just curious; you're finding out what actually holds and then setting down what doesn't. That's the work of this room, and you're doing it with your hand on the pen rather than waiting to feel ready.

The part still open is the pushing-forward part. You think best by inquiring, and this room also rewards someone who decides. Take the ending you've already chosen one step further, without another round of thinking it through. Say the sentence to whoever it concerns, or carry the object that marks it out of the room and set it down somewhere else. The clearing gets to be finished instead of studied, and the ground here is solid enough to stand on while you move.
cells.sheetLine: The question has an answer. Take the step.
cells.verb: turning over each stone with the energy of discovery
cells.place: in the clearing where what was must fully end for what will be to begin

cells.tense: You are bracing for an ending that has not happened yet, pushing the clearing past its own timing.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a small thing this week with no outcome attached — a sketch, a route you haven't walked, a first line — and stop there.
cells.core:
You want the ending finished now — you can see the cleared table and the fresh start behind it, and you're already standing in that room in your head. The thing you're clearing hasn't fully ended yet, so the push you feel isn't cutting anything; it's rehearsing. You keep turning it over, and the turning has an edge of hurry on it that other people can hear.

Begin a small thing this week with no outcome attached — a sketch, a walk somewhere you haven't been, a first line of something. Nothing has to come of it, and you can stop where it stands. You get to feel a beginning from the inside instead of from the far side, and the clearing waits until it's actually done. That's the invitation, and it costs nothing to try.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing before the ending. Start something instead.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that shut behind you, and nobody has asked what's next.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Picture what you'd like to happen next — its shape, not the plan — and feel toward it, sitting with it as long as feels right.
cells.core:
The ending happened, and since then you've been moving through the days without asking much of them. The questions that used to come easily — what is this, what's really here — have gone quiet, and you're not turning much over. From the outside you look settled. From where you sit, the days have less in them than they used to.

It isn't effort that's absent — pushing harder into this wouldn't help. It's the softer thing: feeling toward what comes next, which is slower than deciding. Picture what you'd like to happen — its shape, not the plan — and let yourself want it, sitting with it as long as feels right. What you get is a direction that comes from you rather than from the ending, and the days stop being something you're getting through.

cells.tense: You are the one making the fair call about what ends here, and you call it the timing.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Weigh honestly what an ending costs the people it touches against what it gives them — then make the call knowing it's yours.
cells.core:
You've been making calls in this clearing about what stays and what goes, and the calls have been good — steady, fair to the people involved, not lined with personal score. Asked about it, you'd probably say things have been sorting themselves out, or that the timing was simply right. Somebody has been weighing the costs and the fairness in each one, and that somebody has your handwriting.

Weigh honestly what an ending costs the people it touches against what it gives them — including what it costs you — and then make the call knowing it's yours. Nothing changes about the decisions. What changes is that you're standing next to your own judgment instead of watching it happen. That's all this needs.

attempts.check: The record supports that fresh curiosity is operating in the ending-and-clearing seat; it does not support my phrasing that something 'is already over and you keep feeding it a slot' — the record never says what is ending or how long it has been. A reader could reasonably say the clearing is someone else's decision, not theirs, and that no slot exists. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small physical or calendared act that still teaches where real attention goes, even if my read of the situation misses. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you're keeping the old words on the calendar' — it sounds knowing and could be false; I've cut it so the cell offers a move, not a verdict.
